ideas.title: A top you carved, and the ring
ideas.goal: The player turns a top from a chunk of wood or clay on the lathe (the mouse cuts the profile), spins it in the sand ring, and battles the creatures' tops: the one that wobbles, slows or gets knocked out first loses. How you carved it decides everything: a low wide top spins long, a lopsided one wanders, and a round fat one flips itself upside down and spins on its stem like magic. Fun because each top is a design you test in seconds, and losing tells you what to carve next.
ideas.toward: A thing made by hand that behaves by its own real shape and mass: the profile you cut is the inertia, the balance and the tip it spins on.
ideas.idea: The top's mass, centre and inertia tensor computed from the mesh the player cut (wood or fired clay density); a rigid body spinning on its tip with sliding and rolling friction against the sand, so it precesses, nutates, rises, and a near-spherical top does the real tippe-top inversion; tops collide in the ring with contact (PrintSim affine bodies and IPC contact on Mantle). Someone watching sees Lumi shaping a top, then two tops clash in the ring, one wobbling down in widening circles.
ideas.form: A lathe at the workshop and a top ring on the meadow (plugins), the creatures each with their own carved tops; a traced film of a three-round battle and the flip.

ideas.title: The strongest drop on the island
ideas.goal: Drip molten glass into the pond and fish out tadpole-shaped drops; how hot the glass and how cold the water decide how tough the head is. The player tests each drop under the stone hammer, harder and harder, against the creatures' drops: the head shrugs off blows a marble would not, until the tail is snipped and the whole drop bursts into glittering powder in one instant. Fun because it is a contest of making, with a reveal nobody believes.
ideas.toward: A material that keeps what was done to it as hidden stress: how it was quenched decides how it breaks.
ideas.idea: Each drop's shape from a falling viscous blob; its residual stress from a real quench solve (radial heat flow with viscoelastic structural relaxation, so the skin freezes in compression and the core in tension, by how fast it cooled); the hammer blow's contact stress against that skin decides whether the head holds; snipping the tail starts a crack that runs only where the solved tension is, branching at ~1.5 km/s, with fragment sizes from the stored elastic energy. Filmed traced in slow motion.
ideas.form: A plugin at the pond (drip, hammer, snip, the creatures' contest) and a slow-motion traced film of a head holding under the hammer and then bursting from the tail.

ideas.title: An ocarina from a ball of clay
ideas.goal: The player hollows a ball of clay, pokes holes with a stick where they like, fires it, and plays it: covering holes changes the note, and it plays whatever notes the holes made, not a scale someone chose. Then they play a tune and the friends hum it back. Fun because you make your own instrument and find its song.
ideas.toward: Clay shaped by hand that sounds by its own shape: the cavity and holes the player made are the instrument.
ideas.idea: The ocarina's pitch from its real geometry as a Helmholtz resonator (cavity volume from the mesh, each open hole's area and wall thickness as the neck), recomputed as holes are covered; the sound synthesised as a driven resonator with breath noise, played through the game's voice; firing shrinks the clay a little so the notes come out slightly different from the wet one. Someone watching sees Lumi poke holes and hears a crooked little tune.
ideas.form: A plugin at the potter's bench and a traced film with sound of making and playing it.

ideas.title: Lever the boulder
ideas.goal: Lumi wedges a branch under a boulder on the hill, a stone as fulcrum, and the player leans on it: a green branch bows and springs, the boulder rocks, lifts, and rolls downhill through the bushes into the sea in a burst of spray; a dry branch snaps at the worst moment. Fun because moving something a hundred times your weight by leverage feels powerful, and where it rolls is never the same.
ideas.toward: Wood as a tool that works by what it physically does, and the island's heavy things moved by hand.
ideas.idea: The branch as an elastic rod (PrintSim rods on Mantle) with stiffness and break strain by its moisture, loaded at three contacts (fulcrum stone, boulder, Lumi's weight); the boulder a rigid body from its own mesh rolling and bouncing on the terrain, crushing bushes and splashing into the sea. Someone watching sees a branch bend under a small bird and a big rock tumble away.
ideas.form: A Jump in plugin on the hill and a traced film of a boulder rolled into the sea.
